text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-acme-01' GPU capacity exhausted for tenant AcmeCorp. GPU util=99%, queue_length=312, avg_latency_tokens=2.1s, errors: 5xx spike. Pager -> @oncall-sre. Incident ID INC-2026-0423-01

alex.sre: Paging in. I see the same in the dashboard. Dedicated node count at 24/24, autoscaler not kicking due to pool cap.

priya.platform: Confirmed. Pool has a hard cap from the reserved contract. Autoscaler hit max. Metrics: 
```
pool_id: dedicated-acme-01
nodes_total: 24
nodes_active: 24
pending_queue: 312
avg_q_time: 42s
errors_5xx_1m: 78
```

jamie.runtime: Looks like one tenant (AcmeCorp) is responsible for nearly all active allocations. We have per-tenant isolation but their long-running streams pinned a lot of KV cache memory so nodes can't pack more.

alex.sre: Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle new requests for AcmeCorp at routing layer, 2) enable spillover to shared burst pool (if allowed by contract), 3) ask Acme to reduce parallel streams, 4) manual scale up (requires approval) or evict lower-priority jobs.

tanya.cs: I'm on a call with Acme. They're seeing 502s and timeouts in production for a subset of routes (batch generation). They're urgently asking for a workaround. Legal/contract note: their Dedicated plan doesn't include unlimited burst; need finance sign-off for extra reserved capacity.

liam.solutions: Could we route only non-sensitive requests to hosted fallback? Acme has a VPC/private requirement for some routes, but non-sensitive telemetry could go to hosted for immediate relief. Need opt-in from Acme.

alex.sre: Good idea. Two parallel actions: (A) immediate routing throttle + hosted-fallback for non-sensitive paths, (B) engage go/no-go on one-time burst capacity (spin up 4 gpus in us-west temporary).

priya.platform: To spin up burst we need billing flag and infra approval. Ops can create temporary burst if account team signs off. I can prepare the infra change: 
```
# temp scale command (dry-run)
rictl pool scale --pool dedicated-acme-01 --add-nodes 4 --runtime gpu-a100
```

jamie.runtime: Also we can evict non-critical jobs that are older than 10m from that pool and consolidate KV caches: 
```
kubectl get pods -l tenant=acmecorp,priority=low -o name | xargs kubectl delete
```
This will free ~2 nodes worth of capacity if successful.

alex.sre: I'm going to throttle at gateway for now. Priya, can you prepare the burst request? Tanya, tell Acme we're enabling throttling and asking them to opt-in to hosted fallback for non-sensitive routes. Liam, coordinate which endpoints are safe to fallback.

priya.platform: On it. Opening infra request and tagging finance. Request prepared: INFRA-REQ-8243. Adding devops-bot to run validation.

devops-bot: Validation check complete: burst template OK, but KMS keys for Acme-hosted fallback missing from hosted account. Hosted-fallback will be allowed only after KMS policy is set.

tanya.cs: Acme approves the hosted fallback for those endpoints and can temporarily pause a few high-parallel feeds. They asked us to prioritize stability over throughput.

alex.sre: Throttle rule deployed (gateway): new sessions for tenant AcmeCorp limited to 60 reqs/min per org. Observability: queue_length dropping from 312 -> 198 in next 3m.

priya.platform: Finance approved one-off burst for 4 GPUs. Spinning up nodes now. Command issued: 
```
rictl pool scale --pool dedicated-acme-01 --add-nodes 4 --ticket INFRA-REQ-8243
```

jamie.runtime: Eviction ran: removed ~18 low-priority pods, freed 2 nodes worth. After burst nodes come up, we should have ~6 extra node-equivalents. Watch for KV cache warmup.

liam.solutions: Verified hosted fallback endpoints and updated routing table for /v1/generate-bulk -> hosted fallback. Added header x-tenant-privacy: non-sensitive.

alex.sre: Handing off to next on-call at 1872504520 (in 15m). Current state: queue_length=44, errors_5xx_1m=3, latency back to 0.9s for served requests. Ongoing tasks: Priya to confirm burst node health, Jamie to monitor KV cache pressure, Tanya/liaison to confirm Acme customer UX.

priya.platform: Burst nodes healthy, joined cluster at 1872504558. Node metrics: GPU util settling at 50-65%.

tanya.cs: Acme on the call says errors are almost gone and timeouts reduced. They're happy with hosted fallback routing. Will follow up on a permanent higher burst cap as part of contract renewal.

alex.sre: Closing active paging loop. We'll keep the thread open for post-incident notes. Next steps: postmortem draft (owner: jamie.runtime), propose per-tenant guardrails (owner: priya.platform), update runbook for contract-triggered burst (owner: tanya.cs).

devops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423-01 transitioned to MONITORING state at 1872504689.
